method: Selected episodes with an explicit policy-tool announcement or commitment in the linked original. The reading describes the tool, its timing and its conditions. The prospective policy-rate score is recorded separately. Other announcements and contemporaneous news may move prices in the same window. The selection is illustrative and cannot establish how often each tool was used.

records.evidence: The FOMC added up to $750 billion to its agency mortgage-backed securities purchase programme and authorised up to $300 billion of longer-dated Treasury purchases over six months. Those figures were ceilings on future purchases.

Trichet announced 12-month loans to banks at a fixed rate with full allotment. The ECB would set the first operation’s rate equal to its main refinancing rate. This lengthened the funding available against eligible collateral.

The FOMC planned $400 billion of purchases of Treasuries with six to 30 years remaining and equal sales of securities with three years or less. This operation changed the maturity mix while keeping the two legs equal in size.

records.reading: Signalled readiness to protect the euro
records.evidence: Draghi linked part of the premium on sovereign borrowing to the risk of euro convertibility and put that risk within the ECB’s remit. The speech pledged readiness to act. It specified neither purchases nor a policy-rate path.

records.reading: Set conditions for sovereign bond purchases
records.evidence: Draghi set out how Outright Monetary Transactions could support policy transmission in sovereign bond markets. An appropriate euro-area rescue programme and compliance with its conditions were prerequisites. The announcement established a facility without announcing purchases.

The FOMC began buying an additional $40 billion of agency mortgage-backed securities per month. Continued purchases and possible additional measures depended on progress in the labour market in a setting consistent with price stability.

records.reading: Reduced the pace of net buying
records.evidence: For January, the FOMC lowered monthly agency mortgage-backed securities purchases from $40 billion to $35 billion and Treasury purchases from $45 billion to $40 billion. Holdings would continue to grow, and principal reinvestment continued.

records.reading: Ended net purchases and retained reinvestment
records.evidence: The FOMC ended the purchase programme in October. It would reinvest principal from agency holdings and roll over maturing Treasuries, keeping the portfolio at a sizeable level.

records.reading: Added public debt to an expanded programme
records.evidence: Draghi announced €60 billion of monthly public- and private-sector purchases combined, including purchases of public debt from March. The planned horizon ran to at least September 2016 and depended on a sustained adjustment in inflation.

records.reading: Announced a new series of targeted loans
records.evidence: The Council announced four targeted four-year refinancing operations, starting in June. Participating banks could borrow at a rate as low as the deposit facility rate. The funding terms were one part of a wider package.

records.reading: Signalled a conditional taper and end to net buying
records.evidence: The Council expected to halve monthly net purchases from €30 billion to €15 billion after September and end net purchases after December if incoming data confirmed its inflation outlook. It also intended to reinvest maturing principal.

The Council decided to restart net purchases in November at €20 billion per month. It expected the programme to run while needed to reinforce its rate policy and to end shortly before it began raising rates.

The Council added €600 billion to the pandemic emergency purchase programme, taking its envelope to €1.35 trillion. That amount described the programme’s overall capacity. Purchases could vary across time, asset classes and jurisdictions.

records.reading: Linked continued buying to economic progress
records.evidence: The FOMC committed to adding at least $80 billion in Treasuries and $40 billion in agency mortgage-backed securities per month until it judged that the economy had made substantial progress towards its employment and price goals.

records.reading: Set a start date for reducing holdings
records.evidence: Alongside its rate increase, the FOMC announced that reductions in Treasury, agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities holdings would begin on 1 June. The announcement date and the start of runoff were four weeks apart.

Alongside a 50 bp rate rise, the Council approved the Transmission Protection Instrument. It could buy securities if disorderly market conditions impaired policy transmission. Purchase size would depend on the threat. The decision created the instrument without announcing its activation.

records.reading: Scheduled partial reinvestment for the APP
records.evidence: From March 2023 the Council planned to reinvest only part of the principal maturing under the asset purchase programme, reducing that portfolio by an average of €15 billion per month through June. Pandemic programme reinvestment had a separate timetable.

From June the FOMC cut the monthly Treasury redemption cap from $60 billion to $25 billion. The agency debt and mortgage-backed securities cap stayed at $35 billion. The balance sheet would keep shrinking at a slower pace.
